newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs firmer but downside lingers.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs firmer but downside lingers.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures edged up as players covered their short positions in trade thinned by holidays in London and the United States on Monday.
Dealers said the market remained vulnerable to further tests of the downside after comments by key Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara late on Friday.
Sakakibara told the French daily, Le Monde, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) could be expected to hike its discount rate by 0.50 percent in the coming year.
The lead December Euroyen contract was quoted at 98.89 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 98.87 after falling to a low of 98.86 last Friday. Volume was a light 3,649 lots.
"I'm still looking for levels to sell the Euroyen," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
He said the December contract was likely to remain capped at 99.00 but could head as low as 98.75, if support at the 98.79 level gave way.
Dealers said the market would monitor Japan's April industrial production data and April jobs figures, due Thursday and Friday respectively, for clues about the economy's health.
June JGBs settled at 123.67 against their previous 123.48. Resistance is seen at 123.85 and support at 123.00.
Eurodollar futures were practically unmoved in sleepy trade due to the U.S. holiday. September finished unchanged against an IMM close at 93.970 on meagre volume of 831 lots.
